the unit of analysis is the player-referee dyad
the analytic sample contains N=107,155 dyads
1,335 dyads (1.24%) had at least one red card event
there are 1,316 unique players in the sample
there are 2,825 unique referees in the sample
18,136 dyads (16.9%) are dark-skin dyads
89,019 dyads (83.1%) are light-skin dyads
dark skin was defined as an average skin tone rating greater than 0.50 on a 0-1 scale
light skin was defined as an average skin tone rating less than 0.50
players with a neutral skin tone rating of exactly 0.50 or missing ratings were excluded
skin tone was coded independently by two blind raters from player photos
inter-rater reliability between the two raters was r=0.92
red card was defined as a binary indicator of whether the dyad included at least one red card across all matches the player and referee encountered each other
height (cm, continuous) was included as a covariate
weight (kg, continuous) was included as a covariate
position, coded as 12 categories, was included as a covariate
league country, coded as 4 categories, was included as a covariate
number of games played together (continuous) was included as a covariate
goals scored by the player in the dyad (continuous) was included as a covariate
yellow cards received in the dyad (continuous) was included as a covariate
mean Implicit Association Test score for racial bias was included as a covariate
mean explicit bias score from a racial thermometer was included as a covariate
21,407 dyads were excluded for missing skin tone ratings (players without photos)
8,989 dyads were excluded for having a neutral skin tone rating of exactly 0.50
8,347 dyads were excluded for missing position data
130 dyads were excluded for missing referee country bias data
the final analytical sample was 107,155 dyads, 73.4% of the original 146,028
skin tone scores were averaged across the two raters
the averaged skin tone score was dichotomized at 0.50
red cards were dichotomized into any versus none
categorical variables were dummy-coded with the first category alphabetically as reference
logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors was used as the method
the logistic model specification included dark skin, height, weight, games, goals, yellow cards, meanIAT, meanExp, and position and league dummies as predictors
standard errors were clustered by player using the cluster-robust (Huber-White) approach
players had an average of about 81 dyads each
the risk difference was calculated via marginal standardization (g-computation) with the delta method for standard errors
predicted probabilities were computed for all observations under both exposure scenarios and then averaged to obtain marginal risks
the conclusion is stated as NOT SUPPORTED
